Canadian gold miner and developer with a portfolio of producing mines in the Americas, including Greenstone in Ontario, Los Filos in Mexico, Mesquite in California and several Brazilian operations, plus the Valentine project in Newfoundland. Sells gold bullion to refiners and bullion buyers, so it is a pure B2B commodity producer. Headquartered in Vancouver and founded in 2009; a mid-tier producer with production in the hundreds of thousands of ounces a year, growing through acquisitions such as Calibre Mining in 2025. Listed on the TSX and NYSE American (EQX). No consumer brand awareness.

Singapore-headquartered developer and owner of renewable energy and waste infrastructure assets, active in the Asia-Pacific region with solar, wind and related projects. Earns money by developing, building and selling or operating power and waste-to-energy assets, with customers being utilities, governments and industrial offtakers. Backed by institutional investors, with a large funding round of about $1.33 billion in November 2020. Infrastructure and project-developer business with little public brand awareness among consumers. Exact current ownership and portfolio should be verified before outreach.

US healthcare services company that helps physician groups and health plans run value-based care, with offerings including Evolent Care Partners for specialty and complex care management and technology-enabled specialty benefit management in oncology, cardiology and musculoskeletal care. Customers are health insurers, Medicaid plans and provider organisations, who pay fees and a share of savings. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, with several thousand staff and annual revenue of roughly $2.5 billion. Listed on the NYSE (EVH) since its 2015 IPO. B2B healthcare brand with low consumer visibility.

Pan-regional digital infrastructure provider formerly known as GTT Infrastructure, bought from GTT Communications in 2021 by private equity firm I Squared Capital and rebranded EXA. Operates long-haul and subsea fibre networks across Europe, North America and Asia, selling capacity, wavelengths and dark fibre to telecom carriers, cloud providers, content companies and enterprises. Headquartered in London and PE-owned, with funding of about $1.3 billion shown for October 2025. Purely B2B wholesale network business with almost no public brand awareness.

Canadian base metals developer building the McIlvenna Bay copper-zinc-gold-silver project in the Flin Flon belt of Saskatchewan, which it expects to bring into production as one of Canada's newer copper-zinc mines. Will sell metal concentrate to smelters and traders, so customers are commodity buyers. Based in Vancouver and listed on the TSX (FOM); has raised large equity and financing packages to fund construction, including about $1.3 billion in total funding shown. Resource company with no consumer visibility.

Italy's largest toy company, founded in 1978 by Enrico Preziosi and still privately held. Designs, licenses and distributes toys and games, with own brands such as Cicciobello and Gormiti and many third-party licences, and operates the Toys Center retail chain of toy stores. Sells to retailers and directly to families, with its biggest market Italy and some presence across Europe. Based near Milan. Strong consumer brand in Italy, especially among children and parents, though largely unknown elsewhere. Funding figure shown dates from 2008.

Fund management company based in Beijing, China, described as a fund manager that offers investment products and asset management services. Crunchbase shows total funding of about $1.28 billion, last dated August 2021, and classifies it under asset management and finance. Customers are presumably institutional and retail investors who pay management fees. It is not clear which Harvest-named group entity this is. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

US home insurance company founded in 2015 that uses property data and smart-home devices to underwrite and prevent losses; products include homeowners policies through its Hippo Home Insurance Program, a managing general agent business and a Spinnaker Specialty carrier. Sells to homeowners directly online and through agents and builders, earning premiums, commissions and fees. Headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with a $1.5 billion valuation at its 2021 funding and a Nasdaq-era SPAC listing on the NYSE (HIPO). Modest consumer brand, concentrated in the US.

Late-stage US biotech founded by billionaire Patrick Soon-Shiong, developing immunotherapies for cancer and infectious disease. Its lead product Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept) won FDA approval in 2024 for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. Revenue comes from drug sales and licensing, with customers being hospitals and oncology clinics and funding largely from Soon-Shiong. Based in San Diego area California; listed on Nasdaq (IBRX) after a 2021 merger with NantKwest. Low consumer brand awareness; known to investors and clinicians.

Canadian gold developer building the Kone gold project in northern Cote d'Ivoire, one of the larger undeveloped gold deposits in West Africa, targeting production in the coming years. Will sell gold bullion to refiners, so it is a B2B commodity business with no products or consumers. Headquartered in Vancouver and listed on the TSX (MAU), with total funding of about $1.2 billion raised through equity and project finance. No consumer visibility; sponsorship fit is limited.

Canadian diamond miner whose main asset is a 49% interest in the Gahcho Kue diamond mine in Canada's Northwest Territories, jointly owned with and operated by De Beers (51%). Sells rough diamonds through De Beers' sales channels to diamond cutters and traders, a B2B model. Headquartered in Toronto and listed on the TSX (MPVD) with a history of heavy debt financing; around $1.2 billion total funding shown. Heavily leveraged commodity producer with no consumer brand awareness.

Zinc-focused mining and smelting company with mines in Peru and Brazil, including Cerro Lindo, Atacocha and Vazante, and smelters at Cajamarquilla in Peru and several Brazilian sites. Sells zinc and by-product metals to industrial buyers and traders. Majority-owned by Brazil's Votorantim group (about 65%) and listed on the NYSE (NEXA) since its 2017 IPO; legal base in Luxembourg and operational headquarters in Sao Paulo. Several thousand employees and revenue around $2.5 to 3 billion. B2B commodity producer without consumer visibility.

US online small business lender that used proprietary credit scoring to offer term loans and lines of credit to small firms within days. Founded in New York in 2006 and listed on the NYSE (ONDK) in 2014; acquired by Enova International of Chicago in October 2020 for about $90 million, after which it operates as an Enova brand. Customers are small and medium businesses, earning interest and fees. Funding shown includes debt facilities. Moderate B2B brand recognition among US small business owners.

Canadian precious metals royalty and streaming company, formerly named Osisko Gold Royalties and renamed OR Royalties in 2025. Holds royalties and streams on gold mines, with its cornerstone asset a royalty on Canadian Malartic in Quebec, plus interests in other mines in Canada, the US and elsewhere. Earns revenue from mine operators' production without running mines itself. Based in Montreal and listed on the TSX and NYSE (OR), founded 2014. Investor-focused B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

US medical device company that makes the Tablo hemodialysis system, a portable all-in-one machine aimed at taking dialysis from clinics to acute care hospitals and, potentially, the home. Sells consoles and consumable cartridges to hospitals, dialysis providers and, increasingly, home patients. Based in San Jose, California, and listed on Nasdaq (OM) since its 2020 IPO. Has faced FDA clearance setbacks and raised large venture and public funds. B2B healthcare brand with minimal consumer visibility.

US producer of metallurgical coal for steel makers, with mines in Virginia and West Virginia and a developing rare earth and critical minerals project at Brook Mine in Wyoming. Sells coal to steel producers in the US and export markets and aims to supply rare earths for domestic supply chains. Headquartered in Lexington, Kentucky, founded 2010 and listed on Nasdaq (METC). A mid-cap commodity producer with no consumer brand awareness.

Metal mining company whose Crunchbase entry points to Antofagasta in Chile, consistent with Capstone Copper, a mid-tier copper producer with the Mantos Blancos and Mantoverde mines in Chile and Pinto Valley in Arizona, listed on the TSX (CS) and managed from Vancouver. Sells copper concentrate and cathode to smelters, traders and industrial buyers, so purely B2B. Total funding shown at about $2.49 billion. Not consumer-facing; sponsorship interest would be corporate or reputational rather than commercial. Check which legal entity applies.

Topeka, Kansas, financial services group focused on retirement, with annuity, life insurance and asset management businesses sold through independent advisers, banks and broker-dealers. Customers are individual savers and retirees; revenue comes from premiums, fees and investment spreads. Managing well over $100 billion of assets, and controlled since 2021 by Eldridge Industries, the investment group of Todd Boehly. Sponsors some US sports and community properties but has limited national consumer brand awareness; funding of $1.15 billion was shown for September 2025.

Integrated Canadian steel producer in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, making plate and sheet steel for construction, pipe, automotive and manufacturing customers. Is replacing its blast furnaces with electric arc furnaces to cut emissions, with support from Canadian federal and Ontario government funding. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (ASTL) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Legato Merger Corp. Several thousand employees and annual shipments of about 2 million tonnes. Industrial B2B brand with strong local profile in Sault Ste. Marie and some Canadian sports ties.

London-based business software firm, described by Crunchbase as a leading supplier of SAP Business One and related enterprise software, classified under business intelligence. Presumably sells ERP software, implementation and support to small and mid-sized businesses. The $1 billion funding figure shown looks unusual for a firm of this type and may be an OCR or data error. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Software company behind WordPress.com, WooCommerce, Jetpack, Tumblr, Simplenote and Day One, led by WordPress co-founder Matt Mullenweg. Revenue comes from subscriptions, hosting, commerce plug-ins and enterprise services through WordPress VIP; customers range from bloggers to large publishers. Founded 2005, headquartered in San Francisco with a fully distributed workforce of around 1,900, and valued at about $7.5 billion after a 2021 round. WordPress open-source software runs over 40% of websites. Strong developer and creator brand awareness; ongoing public dispute with WP Engine since 2024.

Major US healthcare distribution and manufacturing company based in Dublin, Ohio, that distributes pharmaceuticals, medical and laboratory products to pharmacies and hospitals, and makes medical products under the Cardinal Health brand. Revenue exceeds $200 billion a year, with around 48,000 employees and a place near the top of the Fortune 500. Listed on the NYSE (CAH). Also runs nuclear pharmacy and at-home care services. Large B2B brand; known to healthcare buyers but little retail consumer visibility.

Carroll County Energy LLC is described by Crunchbase as an energy company based in Westminster, Maryland, active in energy, mining and renewables. Total funding of about $899 million is shown for October 2025, which likely reflects project financing for a power generation asset. Customers are likely wholesale power markets or utilities. The entity appears to be a single-asset project company rather than an operating brand, so its offices, customers and ownership should be confirmed. Likely a B2B energy infrastructure business with no consumer visibility, which limits its relevance as a sponsor. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Former US commercial printing and marketing communications firm headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, making envelopes, labels, forms, custom packaging and printed marketing materials for businesses. Customers were corporate, publishing and financial clients. Grew by acquisitions and was once a large listed company; filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in February 2018 and its operating businesses were then sold off to other buyers. Funding shown of roughly $1.1 billion reflects debt and equity raised over time. B2B printer with low consumer awareness and no longer operating as before.

Melbourne, Australia, health business, described as providing affordable access to health and wellness products. Crunchbase classes it under health care and personal health, with total funding of A$1.6 billion shown for August 2025, which is very large for the sector and likely reflects an acquisition or debt financing. Customers are presumably consumers and retail partners. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chinese national property and casualty insurer based in Shenzhen, Guangdong, offering motor, commercial and other non-life insurance through agents, brokers and online channels. Earns premiums from individual drivers and businesses across China. Total funding shown of about CN 6.45 billion yuan, last dated December 2021, reflecting capital increases from shareholders. A mid-sized domestic insurer with limited brand recognition outside China and modest consumer awareness even inside it.

Regulated electric utility subsidiary of Duke Energy, serving about 900,000 retail customers across most of Indiana from its base in Plainfield. Generates and delivers power from coal, gas, solar and other sources, earning regulated returns on its rate base. Part of NYSE-listed Duke Energy (DUK), one of the largest US utilities. The $1.0 billion funding figure reflects debt or bond issuance in January 2021. Utility brand familiar to Indiana households through local presence, but no national consumer marketing.

Belgian financial market infrastructure group based in Brussels that settles securities transactions and holds securities in custody for banks, brokers and institutional investors worldwide. Operates the Euroclear Bank international central securities depository and national depositories in France, Belgium, the Netherlands and the Nordics. Earns fees from settlement, custody and collateral services, with tens of trillions of euros in assets under custody. Owned by Euroclear Holding, whose shares are held by market users. In the news for holding immobilised Russian central bank assets. Pure B2B with low public awareness.

Newark, New Jersey, private equity firm, described by Crunchbase as investing in businesses and listed with total funding of about $1 billion as of June 2025, which likely refers to capital raised for its funds. Customers and portfolio focus are not specified in the available data, and industry tags are blank. As a private equity manager it is a financial investor rather than a consumer-facing brand, and its sponsorship interest, if any, would be tied to investor relations and relationship hospitality. Its portfolio, fund size and team are not described in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Indian renewable energy developer and independent power producer based in New Delhi, with solar, wind and hybrid projects and clean power supplied to industrial and corporate customers as well as utilities. Part of the Hero Group, the Munjal-family conglomerate behind Hero MotoCorp, and backed by outside investors including a Dutch pension fund-led consortium. Founded 2012. Total funding of about $1.06 billion shown for October 2025. The Hero parent name is a strong consumer brand in India, though the energy arm itself is B2B.

Chinese game live-streaming platform based in Guangzhou, where viewers watch esports and gameplay and tip streamers; revenue comes from virtual gifts, subscriptions and advertising. Spun out of YY (now JOYY) and listed on the NYSE (HUYA) in 2018, with Tencent as the largest shareholder. Has tens of millions of monthly active users in China and a growing esports presence. About $1.1 billion in funding shown, largely from a 2020 Tencent-led round. Strong youth and gamer brand in China, little known elsewhere.

Singapore-headquartered social video and live-streaming group formerly called YY Inc., renamed JOYY in 2020. Main products are Bigo Live, Likee and Hago, with a strong user base in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and other emerging markets; revenue comes from virtual gifts and advertising. Sold its Chinese YY Live business to Baidu for about $3.6 billion in 2020 and spun off Huya earlier. Listed on Nasdaq (YY). Large consumer reach through apps, but brands such as Bigo Live are known mainly to users, not the mainstream.

US midstream oil and gas business, formerly Midcoast Energy Partners, with natural gas gathering, processing and liquids pipeline assets in Texas, Oklahoma and the Gulf Coast. Backed and controlled by Enbridge Energy Partners; the partnership was listed on the NYSE (MEP) in 2013 before Enbridge took it back in 2017. Based in Houston. Customers are producers and shippers who pay fees for gathering, processing and transport. Funding shown of $1 billion dates from January 2020. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

UK digital business bank founded in 2015 by Rishi Khosla and Joel Perlman, lending to growth-stage small and mid-sized businesses and property developers using data-driven credit analysis. Also licenses its credit software. Customers are entrepreneurs and mid-market firms, with earnings from loan interest. Headquartered in London; investors include SoftBank, Clermont Group and GIC, with a valuation near $2.8 billion in 2019 and a major funding round in 2021 of roughly $440 million. Expanded into the US through acquiring a bank. Strong profile among UK business owners and fintech observers.

Gold mining company developing and operating mines in the Americas, including Camino Rojo in Mexico and the South Railroad project in Nevada, and acquired the Musselwhite mine in Ontario from Newmont in 2025. Sells gold to refiners, a B2B commodity business. Headquartered in Vancouver and listed on the TSX (OLA) and NYSE American (ORLA). Total funding shown of about $990 million, last in December 2025. Mid-tier miner with no consumer brand awareness.

Australian gold miner based in Subiaco, Perth, operating mines in West Africa including Edikan in Ghana and Sissingue and Yaoure in Cote d'Ivoire, with the Nyanzaga project in Tanzania under development. Sells gold bullion to refiners and typically produces about 500,000 ounces or more a year. Listed on the Australian ASX and TSX (PRU). Total funding shown of about $878 million, last in December 2025. B2B commodity producer with no consumer brand profile.

US residential property technology and lending firm based in Dallas, Texas, which helps homebuyers make cash offers and finance purchases through its mortgage and buy-before-you-sell products. Customers are home buyers and sellers, earning fees and interest. Total funding of about $905 million shown, mostly from debt facilities, with the latest in September 2021. A fintech-style consumer property brand with limited national awareness; verify its current status before outreach.

Virtual and hybrid events platform that was formerly Hopin, the UK-founded startup that peaked at a roughly $7.7 billion valuation in 2021 after raising more than $1 billion. RingCentral, the cloud communications company, bought the Hopin events business in 2023 and rebranded it RingCentral Events. Customers are enterprises and event organisers running webinars, conferences and trade shows. Based in Belmont, California, under NYSE-listed RingCentral (RNG). B2B software with limited standalone consumer awareness.

US value-based kidney care company that manages care for patients with advanced kidney disease and operates in partnership with health plans, nephrologists and Medicare Advantage programmes. Earns revenue as a share of reduced medical costs for the populations it manages. Based in Denver, Colorado, venture-backed, with total funding of about $936 million and a round shown in September 2025. B2B health care provider with minimal consumer brand awareness.

Calgary oil and gas producer focused on light oil in Alberta, notably the Clearwater and Charlie Lake plays, with production of tens of thousands of barrels of oil equivalent a day. Sells crude and natural gas to refiners and marketers. Listed on the TSX (TVE) and also quoted in the US; grew by acquiring Deep Basin assets in 2023. Total funding shown of about $1.0 billion. B2B commodity producer with little public brand awareness.

Vancouver mining company that owns and operates the Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia (75% owned) and the Florence Copper project in Arizona, as well as Yellowhead and other development assets. Sells copper concentrate and cathode to smelters and traders. Listed on the TSX (TKO) and NYSE American. Total funding shown of about $930 million. Mid-sized copper producer with no consumer brand profile.

Mixed-use waterfront development on the Southwest Waterfront in Washington, DC, built by developers Hoffman-Madison Waterfront. Includes apartments, offices, a marina, hotels, restaurants and The Anthem, a live music venue with about 6,000 capacity, plus Pearl Street Warehouse. Revenue comes from leases, hotel and venue operations. Opened in phases from 2017 and a second phase followed in 2022. Funding of about $1.15 billion shown for June 2025 is likely refinancing. A high-profile DC destination brand with strong local consumer and event visibility.

Largest US multi-state cannabis operator by revenue, based in Tallahassee, Florida, with a dominant medical cannabis position in Florida and operations across many other states. Grows, manufactures and sells cannabis through its own dispensaries (around 200) and wholesale, with brands such as Cultivar Collection and Roilty. Acquired Harvest Health in 2021 for about $2.1 billion; revenue near $1.2 billion. Listed on the Canadian CSE (TRUL) and US OTC markets. Consumer-facing brand with strong state-level visibility, but advertising and sponsorship are heavily restricted.

Life insurance and annuity reinsurance group based in Norwalk, Connecticut, that acquires closed blocks of life and annuity business from insurers. Customers are insurers and policyholders in run-off books; revenue comes from managing those reserves and investments. Backed by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, the Canadian pension investor, and has grown by acquisitions. Total funding shown of about $1.04 billion, last in November 2021. B2B financial company with minimal consumer brand awareness.

South Korean company based in the Seocho district of Seoul, described by Crunchbase as a manufacturer and distributor of industrial gases, classified under manufacturing and oil and gas. Funding of about 1.11 trillion Korean won is shown, last dated June 2023, which suggests an acquisition-related financing. Customers are presumably industrial and manufacturing firms. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dallas, Texas, midstream company engaged in natural gas and crude oil gathering and related infrastructure, classified under energy and natural resources. Crunchbase shows total funding of about $750 million as of April 2022, probably private equity capital and debt for building infrastructure. Customers are oil and gas producers who pay for gathering and transport. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chinese renewable energy equipment supplier based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, classified under solar. Crunchbase describes it as a supplier of renewable energy equipment, with total funding of about $729 million shown, last in December 2022. Presumably sells photovoltaic and related equipment to developers and utilities. The name suggests a link to the Chint Group but that is not confirmed in the data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Singapore-based digital payments and commerce company behind Codashop and Coda Payments, which let gamers in Southeast Asia and beyond buy in-game currency and top up mobile games and apps using local payment methods. Customers are game publishers and consumers; revenue comes from payment processing and commissions. Founded 2011; raised a large round in 2022 reported at a valuation of around $2.5 billion, with investors including GIC. Codashop is recognisable among mobile gamers in emerging markets; the parent brand is mainly B2B.

Duplicate row for Coda, the Singapore-based digital payments and commerce firm behind Codashop and Coda Payments, where the brand name has been garbled by OCR. It lets gamers in Southeast Asia and other emerging markets pay for mobile game top-ups with local payment methods, earning fees from game publishers and payments. Founded 2011 and valued at roughly $2.5 billion in a 2022 round that included GIC. Codashop is familiar to mobile gamers, while the Coda corporate brand is largely B2B.

Luxembourg-based real estate group controlled by Czech billionaire Radovan Vitek, owning office, retail and residential property mainly in the Czech Republic, Berlin, Warsaw and other central European cities. Earns rental income and sells assets; a large issuer of corporate bonds. Operates through subsidiaries including Orco Property Group and GSG Berlin. Total funding of about $724 million shown. Property investor with portfolio worth well above EUR 10 billion; low consumer brand awareness outside local markets.

Owner and operator of the high-voltage electricity transmission network in South Australia, based in Adelaide, connecting generators and distributors across the state. Revenue is regulated, set by the Australian Energy Regulator. Owned by a consortium including YTL Power International of Malaysia, the Hastings Funds Management infrastructure fund and State Grid Corporation of China. Total funding shown of about $777 million, last in February 2022. Critical infrastructure with little public brand awareness.

Canadian cleantech company that converts non-recyclable municipal waste into biofuels and renewable chemicals through gasification, with a commercial plant in Edmonton, Alberta and a larger project planned at Varennes, Quebec. Customers are fuel and chemical buyers and municipalities. Based in Montreal; investors have included Suncor, Waste Management, Shell and the Quebec government. Total funding shown of about $820 million, last in April 2022. B2B technology company with limited consumer awareness.

Denver, Colorado, oil and gas company, described by Crunchbase as providing oil and energy products, and tagged with chemical, energy and oil and gas. Total funding of about $732 million is shown, last in July 2022, probably private equity capital for exploration and production assets. Customers are presumably refiners and marketers. As an upstream or midstream energy business it would sell commodity products to other companies and has no consumer brand. Its scale, asset locations and ownership are not described in the data available here, so a short check is needed before approaching. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Australian renewable energy and storage developer based in Sydney, owner of the Kidston Pumped Storage Hydro project in Queensland, the Jemalong solar farm and the Bouldercombe battery. Sells power and grid services to the electricity market. Formerly listed on the ASX (GNX), it was taken private by Japan's J-Power in 2022. Total funding shown of about $862 million, last in February 2022. Infrastructure business with little public brand awareness.

Chinese city gas utility based in Hefei, Anhui province, classified under chemical and manufacturing, focused on supplying natural gas and related products. Crunchbase shows total funding of about CN 4.63 billion yuan, last in July 2022. Customers are households and industrial users in the local gas distribution area. Such utilities are typically regional, local-government-linked businesses with a captive local customer base, so brand awareness is confined to the city and province and it has little reason to sponsor international sport. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Greece's largest energy group, formerly Hellenic Petroleum, which refines crude oil at Aspropyrgos, Elefsina and Thessaloniki and sells fuels through retail brands EKO and Hellenic Fuels (BP in Greece). Also expanding into renewables, power and gas. Listed on the Athens exchange (ELPE); main shareholders are the Latsis family's Paneuropean Oil and Industrial Holdings and the Greek state. Operations in Greece, Cyprus and the Balkans, with revenue of roughly EUR 10 billion a year. EKO is a well-known consumer fuel brand in Greece.

San Francisco-based company described by Crunchbase as offering a digital marketplace built for sellers and shoppers, tagged with digital marketing and e-commerce. Total funding of about $800 million is shown, last in November 2021, which is unusually large and the same name is used by several unrelated businesses. Without a clear sector from the input, it is difficult to tell whether this is a retail, creator or services platform, and the founders, products, customers and ownership cannot be identified from the data provided. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Finnish wind power developer and owner based in Helsinki, which develops, builds, owns and operates onshore wind farms mainly in Finland and other Nordic markets, selling electricity under long-term contracts to industrial buyers and utilities. Founded in the 2010s and backed by institutional investors, with funding of around EUR 700 million shown for November 2023. An infrastructure and project-developer business with little public brand awareness.

London technology company that built SpatialOS cloud simulation technology and has pursued virtual worlds, games and defence simulation. Founded 2012 by Herman Narula and Rob Whitehead; SoftBank invested about $500 million in 2017. Sold its defence business to Bohemia Interactive Simulations in 2022 and shifted towards metaverse and gaming projects such as MSquared and M2. Revenue from software licences and services to game studios, governments and enterprises. Total funding shown of about $852 million. Known in the games industry and tech press rather than to consumers.

Polish industrial and logistics real estate developer, MLP Group S.A., based in Pruszkow near Warsaw, building and leasing modern warehouse and light-industrial parks in Poland, Germany, Romania and Austria. Customers are logistics, e-commerce and manufacturing tenants who pay rent. Listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (MLP). Funding of about EUR 750 million shown, likely bond and loan financing. B2B property developer with low consumer brand awareness.

Nashville, Tennessee, media and entertainment company, shown by Crunchbase as an online platform that offers independent artists tools to reach audiences, tagged with art and media. Total funding of about $730 million is shown, last in April 2022, which is large for such a platform and may reflect a similarly named music business. The brand label also contains OCR noise. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

French neobank for small businesses and freelancers, based in Paris, offering business accounts, cards, invoicing and spend management. Founded 2016 by Alexandre Prot and Steve Anavi, and valued at about EUR 4.4 billion after a EUR 486 million round in early 2022. Serves hundreds of thousands of business customers in France, Germany, Italy and Spain, earning subscriptions and card interchange fees. Funding shown includes a debt facility in August 2022. Well known to European SMEs and sponsors sports and media.

Sugar Land, Texas, oil and energy company listed by Crunchbase under clean energy and energy, with total funding of about $800 million as of May 2022. Likely private equity or debt-backed midstream or energy infrastructure business, though the data does not say what it owns. Customers are presumably producers and marketers. It looks like a private, investor-backed energy infrastructure company serving other businesses rather than a consumer brand, so public visibility is probably low. Its assets, management and ownership are not described in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

One of India's largest private life insurers, a joint venture of State Bank of India (majority owner) and BNP Paribas Cardif, headquartered in Mumbai. Sells term, savings, pension and health insurance through the SBI branch network, agents and online. Listed on the NSE and BSE (SBILIFE) since its 2017 IPO. Millions of policyholders and assets under management above INR 3 trillion. Total funding shown of about $820 million, last in March 2022. Strong consumer brand across India through the SBI name.

Parent of Silicon Valley Bank, formerly the leading US bank for technology startups and venture capital firms. SVB collapsed on 10 March 2023 after a run on deposits and was taken over by the FDIC; First Citizens BancShares then acquired its deposits and loans, and SVB Financial filed for Chapter 11 and later emerged. Based in Santa Clara, California. The funding shown, about $800 million in 2022, predates the failure. Well known in tech, venture and financial circles; reputational baggage from the collapse.

Renewable energy arm of India's Tata Power, based in Mumbai, which develops and operates solar and wind farms and provides engineering and construction work for corporate and utility customers. Backed by the Tata group, with BlackRock Real Assets and Mubadala investing in 2022; funding shown of about $762 million. Capacity in the multiple gigawatts range and growing. B2B power business, but the Tata name is among India's most recognised consumer and industrial brands.

Global technology consultancy founded in 1993 and based in Chicago, which builds custom software and digital products for large enterprises, known for Agile development and its Technology Radar. Chief scientist Martin Fowler is well known among developers. Operates in about 18 countries with around 10,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (TWKS) in 2021 and taken private by Apax Partners in 2024. Customers are banks, retailers and public bodies. Funding shown of about $748 million, last in January 2021. Respected B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Pan-African banking group headquartered in Johannesburg, formerly Barclays Africa Group, which Barclays reduced its stake in from 2017. Offers retail, business, corporate and investment banking plus insurance and wealth management across South Africa and about ten other African markets. Millions of customers and tens of thousands of staff. Listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (ABG). Sponsors sport including the Absa Cape Epic mountain-bike race and South African rugby and golf. Funding shown relates to a 2023 capital raise. Major consumer-facing banking brand in South Africa.

Residential property developer headquartered in Stockholm, spun out of the Swedish construction group NCC in 2016. Builds and sells apartments and houses to homebuyers in Germany, Sweden, Finland, Denmark and the Baltics, with Germany the largest market. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Annual output has been in the thousands of homes, with revenue in the billions of Swedish kronor, and the company has recapitalised in recent years. Moderate consumer brand awareness in its Nordic and German markets.

Joint venture between agribusiness giant Bunge and oil major Chevron, formed in 2022 to produce lower-carbon-intensity vegetable oils from soybeans and canola as feedstock for renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel. Builds and operates new oilseed crushing capacity, including at Destrehan in Louisiana, with the products sold into fuel-making. Based in San Ramon, California, where Chevron is headquartered. Funding of about $600 million is shown for May 2022. B2B energy-agriculture venture with no consumer visibility, though both parents are well known.

UK clearing bank that gives banks, building societies and fintechs direct access to payment schemes through APIs, founded in 2015 by Charles Delingpole and launched in 2017. Customers are other financial institutions that use its accounts and payment services, as well as some corporate clients. Based in London and backed by investors including Hume Capital and others; funding shown of about $627 million, last in March 2022. Well known in crypto circles, with limited mainstream consumer awareness and regulatory risk.

Hong Kong's first virtual life insurer, licensed in 2018 and backed by Guardian Group, Pacific Century Group and other investors, selling term life and medical insurance online at lower prices. Based in Wan Chai. Customers are individuals buying cover through its website and app. Funding of about $158 million shown. Modest brand awareness among younger digital-first buyers in Hong Kong.

Ohio community bank headquartered in Sandusky, the subsidiary of Civista Bancshares (Nasdaq: CIVB), providing personal and business banking, commercial lending, wealth management and leasing across Ohio and neighbouring states. Assets are about $4 billion. Funding of about $155 million shown. Regional consumer brand with strong local awareness in northern Ohio and community sponsorships. Customers are households, farms and businesses in Ohio and southeast Michigan, and the bank grew through acquisitions.

Canadian clean technology company, based in Calgary and listed on the TSX (EXRO), that makes the Coil Driver power electronics for electric motors, allowing them to switch between efficiency and torque modes, and Cell Driver battery technology. Customers are vehicle makers and equipment manufacturers. Funding of about $158 million shown. B2B technology brand, known in electrification circles but not to consumers.

Professional networking site and recruiting platform, founded in 2002, with over a billion members. Revenue comes from recruiting products, premium subscriptions, learning and advertising. Acquired by Microsoft in December 2016 for about $26 billion and operating as a Microsoft subsidiary, with its main offices in Sunnyvale, California. Funding of about $155 million shown reflects its earlier private rounds. One of the best-known professional brands, widely recognised by workers and employers globally.

Arlington, Virginia, company described by Crunchbase as Minting Technologies, a Delaware business operating in renewable energy and solar. Total funding of about $150 million is shown. The name is shared by many firms, including the personal finance app Mint, so this entry should be confirmed. Customers and products are not described in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

US financial technology company founded in 2016 in San Francisco that lets immigrants carry their credit history across borders, using partnerships with credit bureaus abroad to help lenders, landlords and employers evaluate newcomers. Also offers credit data tools for lenders. Customers are banks, fintechs and property managers. Funding of about $159 million shown. B2B brand, well known among lenders and immigrant communities.

UK renewable developer based in Houghton le Spring, Tyne and Wear, described by Crunchbase as a developer of onshore wind farms and cleantech projects. Total funding of about 120 million (currency not shown, probably pounds) is listed. Projects, ownership and customers are not described. A B2B project developer with no consumer awareness. It is likely a small developer, so its public profile would be mainly among landowners, local planners and energy investors. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

US space technology company based in Colorado Springs, selling space domain awareness data, satellite tracking and analytics and simulation training tools to defence and commercial customers, including the US Space Force. Owns a network of ground-based optical sensors and software such as Slingshot Beacon. Venture-backed, with total funding of about $151 million shown. B2B brand known in the space and defence industries.

Singapore telecommunications and media group, StarHub, providing mobile, broadband, fixed and pay-TV services to consumers and enterprises, listed on the Singapore Exchange. Started in 1998 as Singapore's third mobile operator. Millions of mobile subscribers and a significant pay TV base, with sports content. Funding of about SGD 200 million shown, likely bonds. Strong consumer brand in Singapore with active sponsorship and sports broadcasting tie-ins.

US nuclear energy developer based in Charlotte, North Carolina, working on the Integral Molten Salt Reactor, a small modular design intended to produce clean heat and power. Went public via a SPAC merger in 2025. Customers would be utilities and industrial users. Funding of about $157 million shown. Known in the nuclear and investor communities, with early-stage commercial prospects and minimal general consumer awareness.
